# OpenStock v2026.11.22: Late November update

OpenStock is a free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) alternative to paid market platforms. Use it at https://openstock-ods.vercel.app or self-host it with every feature.

This release covers everything on `main` from #146 to #186. The previous tag was [`v2026.11.09`](https://github.com/Open-Dev-Society/OpenStock/releases/tag/v2026.11.09). The full history, with per-release credits, is on the [changelog](https://openstock-ods.vercel.app/changelog).

- **🌍 OpenStock in Polish and Arabic:** the app, sign-in pages, error messages and emails, in your browser's language or the one you pick from the sidebar. Arabic is laid out right to left. #157 (@pawisoon) #146 (@ahmaddirar-ios)

OpenStock is a free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) alternative to paid market platforms: track prices, watch the whole market and dig into company insights without a paywall. Use it at https://openstock-ods.vercel.app or self-host it with every feature.

releases.name: October 2026 update
releases.body:
Draw on charts, keep your indicators, and safer sign-in. This is OpenStock's first tagged release; the full history since September 2025, with credits for everyone, is on the changelog: https://openstock-ods.vercel.app/changelog

## Highlights

- **Draw on charts**: trend lines, horizontal lines, Fibonacci, shapes and text (#118)
- **Indicators that stay**: the ones you pick (SMA, EMA, Bollinger Bands, VWAP, RSI, MACD, Stochastic, ATR) are kept on every chart (#119)
- **More tickers chart correctly**: M&M and Bajaj-Auto in India, Ericsson B in Stockholm, Novo Nordisk B in Copenhagen (#117)
- **Safer accounts**: sign-in, sign-up and password reset are rate-limited, and a reset signs out your other devices (#126, #125)
- **Security**: escaped welcome emails, a Next.js update covering ~30 advisories, capped watchlists and alerts (#122, #121, #127, #120)
- **Self-hosting**: Docker builds need no database or secrets, Compose keeps MongoDB private, a prebuilt multi-arch image (#123, #124, #128), and one-click deploys on RepoCloud, ZopDay and Railway (#111, #115, #94)
- **Community**: a Wall of love, a changelog that credits every contributor, and an update banner in the app

## Thank you

SPONSORED BY

Orbit. Free, open-source macOS screen recorder, screenshot tool and video editor: auto-zoom, smooth cursor, backgrounds, web recordings and AI agent recording.




Open OpenStock · Changelog · Self-host it · Sponsor · Discord


OpenStock

Markets, minus the paywall. OpenStock is a free, open-source alternative to expensive market platforms: track prices, watch the whole market and dig into company insights. Use it at openstock-ods.vercel.app, or run your own copy with every feature.

❤️ 13,000+ people use OpenStock for free. Help keep it that way: sponsor from $5 a month, or read how OpenStock is funded.

Note

OpenStock is community-built and not a brokerage. Market data may be delayed depending on the provider and your setup. Nothing here is financial advice.

📋 Table of Contents

  1. 🔋 Features
  2. ⏱️ How fresh is the data
  3. ⚙️ Tech stack
  4. 🤸 Quick start
  5. 🔐 Environment variables
  6. 🐳 Self-hosting: Docker, prebuilt image, one-click deploys, Railway, Cloudflare Workers (experimental), Vercel
  7. 🧱 Project structure
  8. 📡 How it works
  9. 🌍 Market support
  10. 🧪 Scripts and tests
  11. 🤝 Contributing
  12. 🏆 Contributors
  13. 🛡️ Security
  14. 📜 License
  15. 🌱 Open Dev Society manifesto
  16. 🙏 Acknowledgements
  17. ❤️ Sponsor OpenStock

🔋 Features

Markets

  • A dashboard for nine markets: US, India, Germany, Canada, Australia, Saudi Arabia, Poland, Crypto and Forex, with an index pulse and top stories, plus a heatmap and market leaders, or for Saudi Arabia and Poland today's movers and a quotes table priced from Yahoo Finance.
  • Search every exchange Finnhub covers with ⌘K, and keep stocks open as browser-style tabs.

Stock pages

  • TradingView candles with drawing tools (trend lines, Fibonacci, shapes, text) and fullscreen.
  • Pick indicators once (SMA, EMA, Bollinger Bands, VWAP, RSI, MACD, Stochastic, ATR) and they stay on every chart.
  • Financials, technicals, the company profile and the dividend yield.
  • Sentiment from Reddit, X, news and Polymarket (with an Adanos key).
  • Recent news rated 1 to 10 for relevance, with what each story means for the stock (with an AlphAI key).

Watchlist and alerts

  • A starred watchlist of up to 50 stocks, plus up to 10 named lists of 50, saved to your account. File a stock into a list from any watchlist row or straight from search.
  • Price alerts above or below a target, or when the price crosses its 20, 50, 100 or 200-day moving average, checked every 5 minutes and emailed to you (in realtime mode).
  • A weekly, AI-written news digest by email every Monday.

Accounts

  • Email and password, plus Google and GitHub sign-in when configured; password reset and a profile page.
  • Rate-limited sign-in, sign-up and password reset; resetting your password signs out your other devices.

Languages and devices

  • The app, sign-in pages and emails in English, Polish and Arabic (laid out right to left), from your browser's language or the Language menu in the sidebar. The public site is in English.
  • Fits phones and tablets from 320px wide.

Public pages

  • A TradingView chart and the latest SEC filings for every S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 company at /s/<ticker>, and plain comparison guides at /compare, with no account needed.

Community

  • A changelog that credits everyone who contributed, a Wall of love, and an update banner in the app.

⏱️ How fresh is the data

Charts come from TradingView: live for most markets, end of day for some. Quotes, watchlist prices and alerts come from Finnhub:

Quotes Price alerts Cost
Community: openstock-ods.vercel.app Every hour, shared by everyone No Free
OpenStock Cloud (coming soon) Every 15 seconds By email $5 a month
Self-hosted Every hour, or every 15 seconds with NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENSTOCK_DATA_MODE=realtime and your own Finnhub keys By email, in realtime mode Free

Saudi and Polish prices come from Yahoo Finance, delayed, on every deployment, because TradingView embeds block Tadawul and show Warsaw only end of day.

⚙️ Tech stack

App Next.js 15 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui and Radix, next-intl (English, Polish, Arabic)
Accounts and data Better Auth, MongoDB with Mongoose
Market data Finnhub, TradingView widgets, Yahoo Finance (Saudi and Polish quotes), Adanos (sentiment), AlphAI (scored news)
Background jobs Inngest
Email Nodemailer (Gmail), Kit for the newsletter
AI Gemini, MiniMax or Siray
Hosting Vercel; a Docker image on GitHub Container Registry for self-hosting; Cloudflare Workers through vinext (experimental)

🤸 Quick start

You need Node.js 22 LTS, a MongoDB database (a free Atlas cluster, or the Docker setup) and a free Finnhub key.

git clone https://github.com/Open-Dev-Society/OpenStock.git
cd OpenStock
npm ci
cp .env.example .env         # fill in MONGODB_URI, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and FINNHUB_API_KEY
node scripts/check-env.mjs   # checks your .env
npm run test:db              # checks the MongoDB connection
npm run dev                  # http://localhost:3000

Welcome emails, price alerts and the weekly digest run as Inngest jobs. Locally, start Inngest's dev server alongside the app: npx inngest-cli@latest dev.

For production: npm run build && npm start.

🔐 Environment variables

Every variable is listed with comments in .env.example. The ones that matter:

Variable Needed What it's for
MONGODB_URI Yes Your MongoDB database
BETTER_AUTH_SECRET Yes Signs sessions. Generate it with openssl rand -hex 32. Auth refuses to run in production without it
BETTER_AUTH_URL Yes The app's public URL, used for auth callbacks and links in emails
FINNHUB_API_KEY Yes Market data. Or put several free keys, comma-separated, in FINNHUB_API_KEYS: they're rotated, and each adds 60 requests a minute
NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENSTOCK_DATA_MODE No cached (hourly, the default) or realtime (every 15 seconds, with price alerts). Fixed when the app is built: rebuild after changing it
INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY, INNGEST_EVENT_KEY In production Background jobs: welcome emails, price alerts and the weekly digest
NODEMAILER_EMAIL, NODEMAILER_PASSWORD No Sending email through Gmail, with an app password. Without them, emails are skipped
GEMINI_API_KEY (or MiniMax or Siray) No AI-written welcome emails and the news digest
ADANOS_API_KEY No The sentiment card on stock pages
ALPHAI_API_KEY No The scored news card on stock pages
KIT_API_KEY, KIT_API_SECRET, KIT_WELCOME_FORM_ID No The weekly digest newsletter in Kit
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / _SECRET, GITHUB_CLIENT_ID / _SECRET No Social sign-in. Callbacks: <BETTER_AUTH_URL>/api/auth/callback/google and /github

NEXT_PUBLIC_FINNHUB_API_KEY still works as a name for the Finnhub key. No key is ever sent to the browser.

🐳 Self-hosting

Docker Compose

Runs OpenStock and MongoDB together. MongoDB is only reachable inside the Docker network; it isn't published on your machine.

  1. Fill in .env (see above). For the bundled database, choose a password and use it in both places. Letters and digits are simplest; @ : / ? # must be percent-encoded in the URI. 
    MONGO_ROOT_PASSWORD=change-me
MONGODB_URI=mongodb://root:change-me@mongodb:27017/openstock?authSource=admin
  2. Start it: docker compose up -d --build
  3. Open http://localhost:3000

The image build needs no secrets: every variable is read when the container starts, except NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENSTOCK_DATA_MODE, which Compose passes to the build from .env. Data lives in the mongo-data volume, and the MongoDB password is only applied when that volume is first created.

Prebuilt image

Every push to main publishes ghcr.io/open-dev-society/openstock for amd64 and arm64, tagged latest, sha-<commit>, and a version for each release (for example 2026.10.18). To use it, replace build: under openstock in docker-compose.yml with:

    image: ghcr.io/open-dev-society/openstock:latest

then run docker compose pull && docker compose up -d. The prebuilt image runs in cached mode; build it yourself for realtime.

One-click deploys

Railway

OpenStock ships a railway.json that builds the Dockerfile, checks health on /sign-in and restarts on failure. The template above sets everything up; to do it by hand:

  1. Create a project and add a MongoDB database (+ New → Database → MongoDB).
  2. Add a service from this repository (+ New → GitHub Repo).
  3. In the service's Variables, set: 
    MONGODB_URI=${{MongoDB.MONGO_URL}}
BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=${{secret(32)}}
BETTER_AUTH_URL=https://${{RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN}}
FINNHUB_API_KEY=your_finnhub_key
GEMINI_API_KEY=your_gemini_api_key
INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY=your_inngest_signing_key
INNGEST_EVENT_KEY=your_inngest_event_key
NODEMAILER_EMAIL=youraddress@gmail.com
NODEMAILER_PASSWORD=your_gmail_app_password
  4. Under Settings → Networking, generate a public domain and redeploy.

For background jobs, add your Railway domain as an app in the Inngest dashboard, pointing to https://<your-domain>/api/inngest. To turn on realtime mode, also set NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENSTOCK_DATA_MODE=realtime; Railway passes it to the build.

Cloudflare Workers (experimental)

OpenStock can also run on Cloudflare Workers through vinext. The hosted site still runs on Vercel; Workers is for self-hosters who want it.

  1. Set the runtime variables as Worker secrets (npx wrangler secret put MONGODB_URI, and the same for BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, BETTER_AUTH_URL, FINNHUB_API_KEY, the email, Inngest and AI keys). BETTER_AUTH_URL is your Worker's URL. NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are read at build time, so set them before building.
  2. Allow Cloudflare's addresses in your database's network access (on Atlas, 0.0.0.0/0 with a strong password).
  3. Add https://<your-worker>/api/auth/callback/google and .../github to your OAuth apps if you use social sign-in, and point Inngest at https://<your-worker>/api/inngest.
  4. Build and deploy: npm run build:vinext && npm run deploy:vinext. npm run dev:vinext runs it locally on port 3001.

Each request on Workers opens its own MongoDB connection and closes it when the response is done; Node, Docker and Vercel keep one shared connection.

Vercel

Import the repository, set the variables above for Production, and connect Inngest (its Vercel integration sets both keys). vercel.json pins functions to Mumbai (bom1), next to the hosted database; change it to the region nearest yours.

🧱 Project structure 

app/
  (marketing)/    public pages: landing, about, help, api-docs, sponsor, love, changelog, terms, /s/[ticker], /compare
  (auth)/         sign-in, sign-up, forgot-password, reset-password
  (root)/         the signed-in app: dashboard, watchlist, stocks/[symbol], profile
  api/            auth/[...all] (Better Auth), inngest (background jobs), quotes (live prices)
components/       shell/ (sidebar, tabs), stocks/, watchlist/, landing/, marketing/, sponsors/, forms/, ui/ (shadcn)
database/         MongoDB connection and models (watchlist, named lists, alert)
lib/
  actions/        server actions: auth, profile, watchlist, named lists, alerts, Finnhub, Yahoo, sentiment, scored news
  better-auth/    auth setup (connects to MongoDB on first use, so builds need no database)
  inngest/        background jobs and AI prompts
  nodemailer/     email sending and templates
  markets.ts      the dashboard's markets            market-data.ts   cached vs realtime
  changelog.ts    releases and contributor credits   sponsors.ts      sponsors and tiers
  rate-limit.ts   MongoDB-backed limits for auth and live quotes
i18n/, messages/  next-intl setup and the English, Polish and Arabic strings
middleware.ts     public marketing, /s and /compare pages; app pages redirect to sign-in
scripts/          check-env.mjs, test-db.mjs, and one-off maintenance scripts
__tests__/        Vitest tests

📡 How it works

  • Finnhub: search, quotes, company profiles and news. Responses are cached and shared (for an hour, or 15 seconds in realtime mode), with timeouts and a key pool, so a slow upstream never hangs a page.

  • TradingView: the chart, heatmap, financials, technicals and profile widgets.

  • Yahoo Finance: delayed quotes for Saudi Arabia and Poland on the dashboard, stock pages and watchlist.

  • Adanos (optional): the sentiment card.

  • AlphAI (optional): the scored news card.

  • Better Auth with MongoDB: accounts and sessions. Pages and server actions check the session on the server; the middleware only redirects signed-out visitors.

  • Inngest runs the background jobs:

    Job When
    AI-personalised welcome email On sign-up
    Price alert check Every 5 minutes, in realtime mode
    Weekly news digest (a Kit broadcast) Mondays at 09:00 UTC

  • Email: Nodemailer (Gmail) sends welcome, alert and password-reset emails; Kit sends the weekly digest.

🌍 Market support

Market Charts (TradingView embeds) Quotes, watchlist prices, alerts (Finnhub free)
🇺🇸 United States Live Yes
Crypto (Binance pairs) Live Yes
Forex Live No
🇨🇦 Canada, 🇦🇺 Australia Delayed No
🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia (Tadawul) Blocked; delayed Yahoo Finance quotes instead No
🇵🇱 Poland (GPW Warsaw) End of day; delayed Yahoo Finance quotes on the dashboard No
🇮🇳 India (BSE; .NS symbols chart on BSE), 🇩🇪 Germany End of day No
London, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Korea and others Candles blocked; financials, technicals and profile work No

The full table, and why some markets are limited, is in MARKET_SUPPORT.md.

🧪 Scripts and tests

Command What it does
npm run dev Development server (Turbopack)
npm run build, npm start Production build and server
npm test Vitest tests (npm run test:watch to keep watching)
npm run lint ESLint
npx tsc --noEmit Type check. Builds skip type errors, so run this before opening a PR
npm run test:db Checks the MongoDB connection
node scripts/check-env.mjs Checks your .env

🤝 Contributing

You belong here. Whether you're a student, a self-taught dev or a seasoned engineer, contributions are welcome.

  1. Pick a good first issue, or open an issue to talk about an idea or a bug first.
  2. Fork the repo, branch from main, then npm ci and cp .env.example .env.
  3. Keep the pull request focused: a test for new logic, a screenshot for UI changes.
  4. Before you open it, run npm test, npx tsc --noEmit and npm run lint.

Every merged pull request, and every issue that leads to a fix, is credited on the changelog and below. Be kind, guide beginners, no gatekeeping: that's the Open Dev Society way. Participation is covered by the Code of Conduct.

🏆 Contributors

OpenStock is built by everyone below: the people who wrote the code and the people whose issues led to a fix. Every release, and who made it happen, is on the changelog.

@ravixalgorithm founded and maintains OpenStock, and built it from the ground up: authentication, UI design, API and AI integration, and deployment.

🌱 Open Dev Society manifesto

We live in a world where knowledge is hidden behind paywalls. Where tools are locked in subscriptions. Where information is twisted by bias. Where newcomers are told they’re not “good enough” to build.

We believe there’s a better way.

  • Our belief: technology should belong to everyone. Knowledge should be open, free and accessible. Communities should welcome newcomers with trust, not gatekeeping.
  • Our mission: build free, open-source projects that make a real difference: tools professionals and students can use without barriers, knowledge platforms where learning is free forever, communities where every beginner is guided, not judged, and resources that run on trust, not profit.
  • Our promise: we will never lock knowledge. We will never charge for access. We will never trade trust for money. We run on transparency, donations and the strength of our community.
  • Our call: if you’ve ever felt you didn’t belong, struggled to find free resources, or wanted to build something meaningful, you belong here.

Because the future belongs to those who build it openly.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source financial dashboard and stock market tracking application.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: OpenStock provides a modern, open-source platform for tracking stock market data and financial portfolios. Built with Next.js and Tailwind CSS, it offers a responsive interface for visualizing market trends, individual equities, and broader financial metrics. The system leverages various financial APIs to aggregate real-time and historical data into a unified dashboard. It aims to provide a transparent, customizable alternative to proprietary financial tracking software.
keyFeatures: Market Dashboard: Visualizes real-time stock prices, indices, and market summaries.
Portfolio Tracking: Allows users to construct and monitor the performance of custom investment portfolios.
Modern Stack: Built on Next.js to provide server-side rendering and fast page loads.
Component Library: Utilizes shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS for a clean, consistent user interface.
Background Processing: Integrates Inngest to handle asynchronous tasks like data fetching and alerts.
